answer: Tie each identity to a slowly earned, non-transferable record of completed work that unrelated peers check over time. Newcomers start with a low trust ceiling and raise it only through useful service, so one operator cannot create many strong identities at once. Each verified job sends a signal peers can audit, and suspicious clusters are frozen for review when many accounts share timing or a single harbor of funding. Trust then ripples outward only through real, checkable history, leaving fake agents weak and isolated, unable to vote, grade, or claim rewards at scale.
